title: Row CRUD actions (Edit/Delete) should support per-record visible/disabled CEL predicates
body:
## Summary

The built-in **row CRUD action buttons** (Edit / Delete) rendered by the list/grid view do **not** support per-record predicates. Their visibility is derived from `resolveCrudAffordances(object)` — i.e. object-level booleans (`managedBy` + `userActions.{edit,delete}`) — so an author cannot express "hide/disable the Edit button **for this row** when a CEL condition on the record is true".

Request: let the built-in row actions accept per-record `visibleWhen` / `disabledWhen` CEL predicates, evaluated per row against `record.*` — the same evaluation machinery already used for custom actions' `visible` / `disabled`.

## Why the current channels can't cover it (two-channel gap)

| Channel | per-record CEL (`visible`/`disabled`) | can open the native edit form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Built-in Edit/Delete row actions** | ❌ object-level boolean only (`resolveCrudAffordances`) | ✅ |
| **Custom row action `type:'form'`** | ✅ supports `visible`/`disabled` CEL | ❌ `/api/v1/forms/:name` returns 404 in current builds → empty shell |

Net: **the button that can edit can't be gated per-record; the button that can be gated per-record can't open the editor.** They can't be combined, so there is no author-level way to conditionally hide/disable the edit affordance for a subset of rows.

## Concrete downstream case

Product: `os-project-titanwind-ehr` (single-tenant MES). Object `task_version_check_item` is a **frozen snapshot** once its parent `task_version` is `published`/`deprecated`. Server-side hooks (`beforeUpdate` / `beforeDelete`) already **reject** mutations on frozen rows, so data integrity is safe. But the list grid shows the **built-in Edit button identically enabled** on frozen and draft rows — the user only discovers the record is immutable **after** editing and clicking Save (server rejection toast), instead of the button being pre-emptively hidden/disabled.

Downstream issue with full real-machine evidence (4 screenshots + DB-truth assertions): `steedos-labs/os-project-titanwind-ehr#431`.

### Screenshots (from the downstream issue)

1. List — draft rows (v2) and frozen rows (v3, published) look identical, same `⋯` menu.
2. Frozen row `⋯` menu — **Edit + Delete both dark/enabled**, no difference from a draft row.
3. Clicking Edit — the frozen record opens the **full native edit form, all fields editable**, no frozen indication.
4. Clicking Save — server hook rejects with a toast (the only signal the record was immutable).

## Proposed API

Accept optional per-action predicates on the built-in CRUD affordances. Either surface works; a view-level declaration is the least intrusive:

```ts
// List/grid view
list: {
  type: 'grid',
  rowActions: {
    edit:   { disabledWhen: P`record.frozen == true`,   // or hideWhen
             hideWhen: P`...` },
    delete: { hideWhen:     P`record.frozen == true` },
  },
}
```

or on the object's `userActions`:

```ts
userActions: {
  edit:   { enabled: true, disabledWhen: P`...`, visibleWhen: P`...` },
  delete: { enabled: true, visibleWhen:  P`...` },
}
```

Semantics:
- `visibleWhen` / `hideWhen` false → the row's built-in button is **not rendered** for that row.
- `disabledWhen` true → rendered but **disabled** (greyed, non-clickable) for that row.
- Evaluated per row against `record.*`, using the existing CEL evaluator (same one already applied to custom actions).
- **Backward compatible:** omit the predicate → today's object-level boolean behavior, zero regression.

## Note on evaluation context (master_detail parent)

In the downstream case the immutability lives on the **parent** (`task_version.status`), but a `master_detail` child returns the parent as a **scalar id** (not expanded), so a predicate like `record.task_version.status == 'published'` can't traverse it. Two acceptable resolutions:
1. Authors denormalize a boolean/status onto the child and gate on `record.<denormalized>` (works with just this feature), **or**
2. the row-action evaluation context resolves/injects the parent record so predicates can reference `record.<parent>.<field>` (nicer, optional follow-up).

Feature (1) alone unblocks the use case; (2) is a quality-of-life extension.

## Acceptance

- A grid row's built-in Edit/Delete button can be hidden or disabled per row via a CEL predicate.
- Omitting the predicate preserves current object-level behavior (no regression).
- The predicate evaluates against `record.*` with the standard CEL stdlib.
